title: Access Origination Whitelist and Backfill Runbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This runbook defines the process for managing "access origination" whitelists (allow-lists that limit which networks, services, or principals may originate sensitive operations), the safe backfill procedure when whitelist entries need retrospective enforcement, and the evidence collection and retention required for compliance audits. It spans RBAC policy update standards, audit-log requirements, cross-region data residency considerations during backfill, secure-SDLC callbacks for policy changes, and incident-response steps if the backfill or enforcement causes outages.

Intended audience

- Security engineers
- Platform/infra on-call
- SRE and production incident responders
- Compliance and legal reviewers

Scope and definitions

- Access origination whitelist: a policy artifact that restricts which source identities (IP ranges, VPCs, service accounts) may initiate particular high-risk actions (model rollout, dedicated capacity admin, privileged API calls).
- Backfill: a controlled, retrospective enforcement of a whitelist that was created after some actions have already occurred. Backfill includes identification, tagging, and re-evaluation of historical events.
- Evidence bundle: the set of artifacts packaged and retained to demonstrate compliance during audits (policy version, audit events, change approvals, test results).

Principles and constraints

1. Fail-safe first: enforcement must not cause silent data loss or compromise availability. Always prefer a canary phase with observability and automatic rollback hooks.
2. Minimal blast radius: apply enforcement at narrow scope (customer, tenant, or origin subnet) before broad rollout.
3. Auditability: every change must be accompanied by a policy diff, owner approval, automated test results, and traceable audit events.
4. Residency-compliant packaging: evidence bundles for customers with data residency constraints must be stored in the appropriate region and include MD5/SHA256 manifests.

Policy update workflow (high level)

1. Draft policy change in policy repo (repos/policies/access-origination) with clear description and intended scope. Use file naming: access-origination/<policy-name>/vYYYYMMDD-<short>.yaml.
2. Automated preflight tests run in CI: unit-check policy syntax, simulate policy against a sampled event stream, run negative and positive test cases.
3. Security review: approvals required from at least 2 approvers if scope is global; 1 approver if scope is single-tenant. 
4. Canaries: create a canary enforcement (20–100 requests/sec cap) for a 24–72 hour window or 5,000 requests, whichever comes first.
5. Evidence collection and packaging occurs during canary.
6. Gradual roll (50% -> 100%) with 1-hour observe gates and rollback on error thresholds.

Required metadata for any policy change (table)

| Field | Required value | Example |
|-------|----------------|---------|
| policy_id | string | ao-whitelist-model-rollout |
| author | username | mchen |
| owner_service | service name | routing-gateway |
| scope | tenant|region|global | tenant:acme-corp |
| enforcement_mode | dry_run|canary|enforce | canary |
| canary_scope | list string | ip-range:10.20.0.0/16 |
| rationale | free text | limit model rollouts to private VPCs |
| test_manifest | filename | ao-whitelist-model-rollout/tests/manifest-20250401.json |
| approvers | list | [sec-lead, platform-lead] |
| retention_class | standard|audit-long|sovereign | audit-long |

Audit-log requirements

Every enforcement decision and every access decision affected by the whitelist must be recorded in the central audit stream with the following schema fields (this is the canonical minimal set). Logs must be emitted in JSON, newline-delimited (ndjson), and forwarded to the audit collector within 30s of event creation. Retention and residency are enforced by the audit pipeline.

Required audit event fields (examples)

- event_id: uuidv4
- timestamp: 2025-04-01T13:02:53.123Z
- actor: service-account:router@redwood.internal
- origin: ip:10.20.5.12 | vpc:vpc-abc123 | region:us-west-2
- action: model.rollout.initiate
- target_resource: arn:rr:model:acct:region:model-id
- policy_id: ao-whitelist-model-rollout:v20250401
- decision: allowed|denied|deferred|fallback
- decision_reason: matched-whitelist | no-whitelist-entry | policy-eval-error
- policy_snapshot: sha256:...
- request_payload_digest: sha256:...
- trace_id: 4f7e9...

Example CLI to query events for backfill candidates

# Find all "allowed" decisions before policy creation
curl -s "https://audit-query.internal/api/v1/search?q=action:model.rollout.initiate AND timestamp:[2024-01-01 TO 2025-04-01] AND decision:allowed" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_TOKEN" | jq '.hits[] | {event_id, timestamp, actor, origin, target_resource, decision}'

Backfill procedure (step-by-step)

1. Trigger a dry-run backfill scan
   - Run the backfill scanner against the historical audit store to enumerate all events that would have been denied by the new policy.
   - Command (example):
     ./tools/backfill-scan --policy ./access-origination/ao-whitelist-model-rollout/v20250401.yaml --start 2024-01-01 --end 2025-04-01 --output candidates.ndjson
   - Outputs: candidates.ndjson, summary.json (counts by tenant, region, service)

2. Triage and risk classification (automated + manual)
   - Automatically classify by impact: SCORE = (critical_op ? 10 : 5) * (tenant_is_enterprise ? 2 : 1) * (origin_is_public_internet ? 3 : 1)
   - Flag top-10 tenants by projected impact for manual review. Create a JIRA ticket for each tenant with linked candidates.ndjson snippets.

3. Customer communications and residency checks
   - For tenants with residency constraints, engage compliance/legal. Evidence packaging must be stored in the tenant's allowed region. Do not include event payloads that contain PII unless redaction rules applied.

4. Enable controlled canary enforcement for backfill candidates with remediation path
   - For low-impact candidates, schedule a maintenance window and enable enforcement with an automatic rollback hook.
   - For higher-impact candidates, require a manual mitigation plan (e.g., rotate principals, add origin entries, reissue tokens).

5. Execute remediation with test harness
   - For each candidate where remediation is to be applied, execute the remediation in a staging tenant or test instance. Tests must include:
     a) Functional test: reproduce the request and verify expected denial/allow outcome.
     b) Latency & availability test: ensure enforcement layer adds <10ms median and <50ms p95 overhead.
     c) Observability test: validate audit event emitted with decision and policy_snapshot.

6. Evidence assembly and retention
   - Create an evidence bundle containing: policy YAML, policy diff (git), CI preflight logs, test run outputs, audit event extracts for candidates (redacted as necessary), approvals, maintenance window tickets, and signed digest (sha256).
   - Store evidence bundle in evidence-store with object metadata: {policy_id, tenant_id, evidence_date, retention_class, region}. For sovereign tenants, store in tenant-region only.

7. Full enforcement and post-enforcement review
   - Ramp enforcement using the rollout policy: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with minimum 60-minute observation windows and automatic abort on error budget breaches.
   - Post-rollout: run a resilience test and a review meeting with security, SRE, and product owners. Publish the backfill postmortem to related_pages.

Incident response: if enforcement causes an outage

1. Detect
   - Triggered by SLO alerts or manual reports. Error thresholds (sample):
     - >1% global error increase for control-plane API for 5 minutes OR
     - >0.5% increase for any tenant with >1,000 requests/minute for 3 minutes

2. Immediate actions
   - Toggle enforcement to dry_run or disabled for impacted scope via the rollout controller (CLI):
     rrctl rollout abort --policy-id ao-whitelist-model-rollout:v20250401 --scope tenant:acme-corp
   - Notify on-call security and platform via PagerDuty.

3. Forensic evidence collection
   - Snapshot policy state and audit-stream window (t0-10min to t0+30min). Export to forensics bucket with immutable flag.
   - Capture orchestration logs, canary metrics, and rollout events.

4. Post-incident: root cause analysis and evidence delivery
   - Run RCA within 5 business days. Produce a remediation plan and attach evidence bundle. If the incident meets severity threshold for legal notification, route artifacts to Legal with a secure evidence transfer (SFTP over private link).

Controls, SLOs, and thresholds

- Rollout observation window: minimum 1 hour per gate.
- Automated rollback criteria: >0.5% absolute increase in 5xx responses or >2x baseline latency p95 for 10 minutes.
- Audit event delivery SLA: 30s to collector (99th percentile).
- Evidence retention: policy change artifacts retained for 7 years for audit-long class; 3 years for standard; sovereign tenants per contract.

Testing and CI integration

- Policy PRs must include: unit tests, a CI policy-sim job that runs against a 7-day sampled event set, and red-team scenario tests (at least 3 scenarios).
- CI must produce an artifacts URL and signed manifest that is included in the evidence bundle.

Example policy YAML (simplified)

---
policy_id: ao-whitelist-model-rollout
enforcement: canary
canary: 
  start: 2025-04-15T00:00:00Z
  scope: ["ip:10.20.0.0/16", "vpc:vpc-abc123"]
rules:
  - id: allow-private-vpc
    match: origin.vpc in ["vpc-abc123"]
    effect: allow
  - id: default-deny
    match: true
    effect: deny
---

Sample evidence bundle manifest (JSON snippet)

{
  "policy_id": "ao-whitelist-model-rollout",
  "policy_version": "v20250401",
  "evidence_items": ["git-diff.txt", "ci-preflight.log", "candidates.ndjson", "audit-extract-tenant-acme.ndjson"],
  "retention_class": "audit-long",
  "stored_region": "us-west-2",
  "digest": "sha256:..."
}

Operational playbook checklist

- [ ] Policy authored and unit tested in repo
- [ ] CI preflight completed and artifacts uploaded
- [ ] Security approvers signed off
- [ ] Canary configured with scope and abort hooks
- [ ] Audit pipeline test verified
- [ ] Evidence bundle created and stored
- [ ] Communication plan (tenants & internal) executed
- [ ] Post-rollout review scheduled

Ownership and escalation

- Policy author: security-engineering (primary contact)
- Enforcement operator: platform-infra
- Evidence custodian: compliance-team - PagerDuty escalation: sec-oncall -> infra-oncall -> eng-sre-lead

Related procedures and links

- Policy repository: git@repo:redwood/policies.git (access controlled)
- Audit query service: https://audit-query.internal
- Evidence store runbook: /confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/evidence-orchestration-playbook-for-multi-region-compliance-2025

Appendix: quick commands and queries

# CI preflight fetch
ssh ci-runner "/opt/policy-sim/run --policy-file ./access-origination/ao-whitelist-model-rollout/v20250401.yaml --sample-days 7 --out /tmp/sim-output.ndjson"

# Backfill candidates export example
./tools/backfill-scan --policy ./access-origination/ao-whitelist-model-rollout/v20250401.yaml --start 2024-01-01 --end 2025-04-01 --max-results 100000 > candidates.ndjson

# Extract audit events for a tenant (via audit-query)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_TOKEN" "https://audit-query.internal/api/v1/export?tenant=acme-corp&start=2024-01-01&end=2025-04-01&action=model.rollout.initiate" > audit-extract-tenant-acme.ndjson
